title: Ecosystem Resonance Mapping
opening: An interaction depends on people and conditions. Compare two episodes you experienced before deciding what a pattern means.

labels.workedExample: Two meetings, one difference to investigate
labels.illustration: Fictional illustration: the same colleagues discuss a project in different settings.
labels.firstPeopleExample: Two teammates reviewing the same launch checklist.
labels.firstContext: A quiet room, ten minutes, one question at a time.
labels.firstExperience: I could follow the question and felt open and at ease, with little friction.
labels.firstCue: We took turns; I finished my explanation.
labels.secondPeopleExample: The same two teammates plus four colleagues reviewing that checklist.
labels.secondContext: An open shared table, overlapping turns, the same topic, less time.
labels.secondExperience: I found it harder to follow and felt less open, with more friction.
labels.secondCue: Two people began speaking while I was answering.
labels.examplePattern: In this pair, my openness differed across settings. Noise, turn-taking, time or topic fit could contribute; these episodes do not establish why anyone acted as they did.
labels.exampleInquiry: One possible next step is to ask whether everyone wants to try one question at a time in a quieter check-in, then compare what each person reports.
labels.practiceIntro: Use a role or setting instead of a name, or leave identity out. Keep your experience separate from what you observed. A feeling or one interaction does not establish another person’s motive.
labels.peopleAndRole: Who was involved? Use a role or relationship, not a name
labels.experiencedQualities: Your experience: clarity, emotion, openness, friction and ease
labels.observedCue: What did you see or hear?
labels.observedCuePair: What did you see or hear in each interaction? Note first and second separately.
labels.comparison: What pattern or exception appears, and what remains unknown?
labels.nextInquiry: What would you investigate in yourself or the setting?
labels.private: This map is saved as private practice; it does not submit the separate assessment or mark this lesson complete.

source.excerpt: Map relationships and settings. Record the clarity, emotions, openness, friction and ease you experience in each. Compare patterns to identify something to investigate in yourself or the setting.
source.assessmentBoundary: Six required assessment questions remain separate from this private practice. Saving a partial practice draft does not submit the assessment or mark the lesson complete.
